title: Rav Giddel bar Binyamin

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud: bar Minyamin.

He was Rav’s student, as in [Yerushalmi Pesachim 8:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.8.8.7): Rav Chiyya bar Yosef reports Giddel bar Binyamin’s teaching in Rav’s name; in [Yerushalmi Sotah 6:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.6.4.2) the reading is bar Minyamin. Hyman considers it very likely that he is the one called in the Babylonian Talmud Giddel bar Minyomi, as in [Bava Batra 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.39b.4): Giddel bar Minyomi had a protest to make; he found Rav Huna, Chiyya bar Rav and Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvi and protested before them. In [Yerushalmi Bava Batra 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Batra.3.3.8), the statement is in the name of Giddel bar Minyamin. Hyman nevertheless considers it impossible to say that Rav Giddel bar Binyamin is Rav Giddel without further designation, although we find in Pesachim 28b (compare [Pesachim 78b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.78b.5)), “Rav Giddel said in Rav’s name: If he sprinkled, it is accepted,” and this statement is cited in the Jerusalem Talmud there, 8:8, in the name of Giddel bar Binyamin in the name of Rav — because according to the testimony of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak in [Pesachim 107a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.107a.12), he said: “I taught it neither as Giddul bar Menashya nor as Giddul bar Minyoma, but as Giddul without further designation. What is the practical difference? To pose his statements against each other.” Hyman concludes clearly from this that Rav Giddel without further designation is not Giddel bar Minyomi.

Hyman also regards this as clear: they all lived at one time and were Rav’s students. We find in Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 4:3 (compare [Yerushalmi Shekalim 4:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.4.2.3)) Giddel bar Binyamin in the name of Assi. In [Berakhot 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.49a.22), continuing at [Berakhot 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.49b.1): Giddel bar Minyomi was standing before Rav Nachman; Rav Nachman erred (and did not mention [the insertion for] Rosh Chodesh) and went back to the beginning. Rav Giddel bar Minyomi said to him: “Why did the Master do so? Did not Rav Huna say in Rav’s name,” etc.[^3]

notes.text: Saved Davidson Pesachim107a explicitly names RavNachmanbarYitzchak; the supplied ר״ג is disclosed alongside the contextual expansion rather than silently treated as ר״נ. BarMinyamin/Minyomi/Minyoma and unqualified Giddel remain distinct forms. Hyman’s identification/separation argument and apparent counterexample remain intact.

The consulted Pesachim 107a explicitly names Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak and distinguishes unqualified Giddul from bar Menashya and bar Minyomi. The supplied siglum and Binyamin/Minyamin/Minyomi/Minyoma forms remain disclosed. Hyman’s very-likely identification, impossible equation, apparent counterexample and clear conclusions retain their force as his argument, rather than new identity admission.

The consulted Bavli gives Giddel without a patronymic at Pesachim 78b. The parallel Yerushalmi gives Giddel bar Binyamin. The consulted Shekalim places the Assi attribution in 4:2. In the opening exchange on Berakhot 49b the consulted text has Rabbi Sheila transmitting Rav’s ruling, and the discussion subsequently brings in Rav Huna’s report in Rav’s name. Heilprin has separate notices for [Giddel bar Minyomi](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=855&lang=en) and [Giddel bar Binyamin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=856&lang=en). These listings leave Hyman’s identification argument and his apparent counterexample open.
